column6: In the Sichuan Basin, carbonate nodules were collected from the Qianfoya, Shaximiao, Suining, and Lianhuakou Formations. Based on sporopollenin and bivalve assemblages, the Qianfoya Formation is Aalenian–Bajocian in age, and the Shaximiao Formation is Bathonian–Callovian (Meng et al., 2005; Deng et al., 2017). Previous biostratigraphic studies indicate that the Suining Formation is Oxfordian, and the Lianhuakou Formation is Kimmeridgian (Deng et al., 2017). In the Zigui Basin, carbonate nodules were collected from the Qianfoya, Shaximiao, and Penglaizhen Formations. Biostratigraphic constraints indicate that the Qianfoya Formation is Aalenian–Bajocian, and the Shaximiao Formation is Bathonian–Callovian, temporally comparable to the same units in the Sichuan Basin. The Penglaizhen Formation has been proposed as Kimmeridgian, making it contemporaneous with the Lianhuakou Formation in the Sichuan Basin (Dai et al., 2022; Deng et al., 2017). In the Jiyuan Basin, carbonate nodules were collected from the Anyao, Yangshuzhuang, and Ma’ao Formations. The Anyao Formation is Toarcian in age (Yang et al., 2014; Deng et al., 2017). Based on bivalve assemblages of Unio–Margaritifera–Yananoconcha–Ferganoconcha, the Yangshuzhuang Formation is Aalenian–Bajocian (Huang, 2019), and based on ostracod assemblages of Timiriasevia–Darwinula, the Ma’ao Formation is Bathonian–Callovian (Yang et al., 2014; Deng et al., 2017)
